This page compiles the top headlines and critical updates from across Ukraine, offering a real-time snapshot of key developments. Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. All reports are carefully curated from verified sources and KyivPost correspondents on the ground

Britain’s New Russia Sanctions Show Ukraine Has Not Been Abandoned at the Negotiating Table — Britain’s latest sanctions, unveiled on Nov. 12 as European leaders met in Dublin, make it the first country to directly sanction all 10 of Russia’s largest oil producers, the government says. Stepan Stepanenko argues the measures are imperfect but important: they signal that peace talks will not hand Russia a free pass on oil, and that enforcement – not an ever-longer list of names – is what will deny

NATO Troops Rehearse Contested Neman River Crossing in Lithuania — Military personnel from eight NATO countries simulated a contested river-crossing operation across the Neman River near Prienai, Lithuania, on Friday, Nov. 20, as part of the Freedom Shield 26-II exercises. Supported by German Air Force Eurofighter jets, tanks, and aerial and ground drones, infantry crossed on inflatable boats to establish a bridgehead before Dutch military engineers deployed 90-ton-capacity rafts for heavy armor

Ukrainian Artists Present Contemporary Art in Barcelona — The “LOST & FOUND” exhibition opened on Nov. 10, 2026, at Theodora Extra cultural space in Barcelona, bringing together five artists from Ukraine and Spain. The showcase marked the completion of the first FONT Residence program, an initiative aimed at promoting contemporary Ukrainian art internationally and strengthening cultural dialogue between Ukraine and Europe.

Costa Proposes €1.78T EU Budget for 2028-2034, Preserves €100B for Ukraine — European Council President António Costa presented a revised proposal for the EU’s 2028–2034 Multiannual Financial Framework on Saturday, Nov. 21, trimming overall bloc spending by 10 percent (€204 billion) to approximately €1.78 trillion in current prices while preserving up to €100 billion ($109 billion) for Ukraine. Channeled through a dedicated off-ceiling Ukraine Reserve (€88.9 billion in 2025 prices), the funding

Zelensky: NATO Membership Best Security Guarantee, ‘Yalta 2’ Failed in Shenzhen — President Volodymyr Zelensky stated during a Saturday, Nov. 21 chat briefing with journalists that full NATO membership remains the clearest and most cost-effective security guarantee for Ukraine, noting Kyiv has not yet seen formal written “Article 5-style” commitments. Zelensky also said Russian President Vladimir Putin failed to secure a “Yalta 2” redrawing of borders at the Shenzhen summit, and named potential

Did the Ukraine Summit in Berlin Bring Progress? — Commentators across Ireland, Germany, and Romania have expressed skepticism regarding Europe’s geopolitical clout following German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Nov. 19 “Coalition of the Willing” summit in Berlin. The Irish Examiner warns that declarations of unity cannot replace diplomatic leverage if Europe is excluded from setting peace terms, while Germany’s Die Welt argues that European political power must actually exist rather than produce

Zelensky Honors Heavenly Hundred Heroes on Day of Dignity and Freedom — President Volodymyr Zelensky and First Lady Olena Zelenska honored the memory of protesters killed during the Revolution of Dignity at a newly renovated memorial space on Kyiv’s Alley of the Heavenly Hundred Heroes on Saturday, Nov. 21, marking the Day of Dignity and Freedom. In an official address, Zelensky paid tribute to the courage of Ukrainians during the 2004 Orange Revolution, the 2014 Revolution of Dignity, and the o

SpaceX Hires Democratic-Linked Lobbyists Ahead of Starlink Probes — Elon Musk’s SpaceX has retained five lobbyists from bipartisan Washington firm Mehlman Consulting, including several with close ties to congressional Democrats and past administrations, ahead of planned Democratic investigations into Starlink and Starshield restrictions in Ukraine, Fox News reported. The lobbyists began work on Oct. 1 as polls pointed toward a Democratic sweep in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Finland Detects Drone Attack on Russian Cargo Ship in Baltic — Finland’s military detected a drone attack on a Russian cargo vessel in international waters west of Suursaari in the eastern Gulf of Finland on Saturday morning, Nov. 21, setting the ship ablaze and leaving it drifting toward Finnish waters, the Finnish Ministry of Defense announced. Finnish Border Guard units responded to the scene and confirmed the fire posed no immediate danger to other ships, while Helsinki notified NATO and imp

Zelensky Says Next 4-Party Peace Talks Must Deliver Concrete Results — President Volodymyr Zelensky stated during a Saturday, Nov. 21 meeting with British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting that the next round of four-party peace talks involving Ukraine, Europe, Russia, and the US must be more productive and follow a clear agenda with defined minimum and maximum goals. Welcoming the Abu Dhabi agreement to swap over 1,000 Ukrainian prisoners of war, Zelensky urged negotiators to push for an “all-for

There Is Still Time for Congress to Help Ukraine — Ukraine is a dependable and innovative security partner of the US. It is in America’s national security interests to continue to assist Ukraine as a full ally and a battle-tested nation that can improve US military preparedness.

Russia Attacked Ukrainian Bridges 109 Times Before Crimean Bridge Strike — President Volodymyr Zelensky revealed during a Saturday, Nov. 21 meeting with British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting that Russian forces launched 109 missile and drone attacks against Ukrainian bridges prior to Ukraine’s retaliatory operation on the Crimean Bridge, noting extensive evidence of Russian tanks and artillery using the crossing. Concurrently, Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara assessed that Russian di

NATO Cleared Pilot to Shoot Down Russian Missile Over Poland, Held Fire Over Weather — A Swedish JAS 39 Gripen pilot received NATO authorization to shoot down a suspected Russian Kh-101 cruise missile during Friday’s airspace violation over southeastern Poland, but held fire because severe weather prevented visual and optoelectronic identification. Operational Commander Lt. Gen. Ireneusz Nowak said Polish radars tracked 11 potential threats as two cruise missiles and a jet-powered drone crossed

Ukraine Strikes Ammunition Depot in Crimea, Command Posts and Bridge in Occupied East — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine announced on Saturday, Nov. 21, that over the past 24 hours Ukrainian forces struck a Russian ammunition depot near Pervomaiske in occupied Crimea, two unit command posts near Pryshyb in Zaporizhzhia region and Ukrainsk in Donetsk region, and a road bridge across the Siverskyi Donets River near Luhansk.

EXPLAINER: Russia’s Gulag Imperative — Russia’s prison population has fallen heavily since 2021, largely because inmates have been recruited to fight in Ukraine. Yet the Kremlin is launching its biggest prison-building program since Soviet times, including a 4,000-place detention center near Moscow and a complex in occupied Kherson. With the FSB also regaining its own jails, is this a sign of preparation for mobilization, dissent and Moscow’s need for tighter control?

Germany to Allocate €30M Down Payment for ‘Industrial Ramstein’ Program — Germany will provide €30 million ($32.6 million) as an initial down payment for the “Industrial Ramstein” program to help Ukrainian enterprises purchase German equipment and restore war-damaged production. Kyiv aims to finalize the program – alongside Japan, the Netherlands, and Estonia – and launch a €3 billion War Risk Insurance Fund at the January Ukraine Recovery Conference in Tallinn.

Drones Target Russia’s Ust-Luga Baltic Port in Overnight Raid — Dozens of long-range strike drones attacked Russia’s Leningrad region overnight and early Saturday, Nov. 21, sparking explosions near the strategic Baltic Sea export port of Ust-Luga as the Russian Defense Ministry claimed 275 drones were intercepted across 12 regions, occupied Crimea and the Black Sea. Leningrad Governor Alexander Drozdenko claimed 61 drones were downed over the region without confirming ground damage at Ust-Luga,

Russian Ice Dancers Withdraw From Warsaw Cup After Polish Ministry Opposition — Two Russian ice dance couples – Anna Kolomenskaya and Artyom Frolov, and Yekaterina Mironova and Yevgeny Ustenko – have withdrawn from the PGE Warsaw Cup figure skating competition after Poland’s Ministry of Sport and Tourism formally advised against their participation. Although vetted Russian skaters hold neutral status from the International Skating Union (ISU), athletes competing in Poland must sign declarations

Russian Morning Attack on Kyiv Injures 2 Men, Damages Homes — A Russian morning aerial attack on Kyiv injured two men aged 63 and 67 – one of whom was hospitalized – and damaged private residential buildings across the Podil, Holosiivskyi, and Solomianskyi districts on Saturday, Nov. 21, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko and city police reported. Falling debris ignited a fire at a private home in Podil and landed on open ground in Solomianskyi.

European Security Advisors Weigh Moscow Talks After Kremlin Invitation — National security advisors from France, Germany, and the UK could travel to Moscow later in November for talks on ending the war in Ukraine following a proposal by Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov. While no final decision has been made, the German Chancellery pointed to Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s readiness for four-party talks with Ukraine, Russia, Europe, and the US, while French officials insisted Moscow must recognize Europe’s

Zelensky Warns Putin Crimean Bridge ‘Will Not Stay’ — President Volodymyr Zelensky warned during an NBC News interview that the Crimean Bridge “will not stay” and that Vladimir Putin must understand Kyiv will continue retaliating for Russian strikes on Ukrainian bridges and railways. His remarks follow Nov. 17 SBU and Nov. 19 Neptune missile strikes that destroyed a major road arch and damaged railway tracks on the Kerch Strait crossing, leaving road traffic closed for at least one to two months

Melania Trump Expresses Hope for Ukraine-Russia Ceasefire by Christmas — US First Lady Melania Trump stated during a Friday, Nov. 20 Fox News interview that she hopes Ukraine and Russia can reach a new ceasefire by Christmas, noting that talks are ongoing and could succeed quickly if both sides are ready.

European Leaders Condemn Russian Airspace Breach and Pledge Poland Support — European Union, British, and NATO leaders condemned Russia’s overnight violation of Polish airspace on Friday, Nov. 20, after three objects – assessed as two missiles and a drone – entered Poland and a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile came down roughly 60 kilometers from the Ukrainian border. NATO scrambled aircraft in response, while NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte pledged to strengthen alliance deterrence ahead of his

Russian Drone Strike on Kharkiv Region Apartment Block Injures 11 — A Russian strike drone hit a five-story residential apartment building in the settlement of Solonytsivka in Ukraine’s Kharkiv region, injuring 11 people – including two children – and sparking a 250-square-meter fire across the fourth, fifth, and technical floors, the State Emergency Service (DSNS) reported on Saturday, Nov. 21. Blast waves also damaged nearby apartment blocks, private homes, summer cottages, and cars.

Moscow Threatens to Reject Peace Talks Involving EU’s Kaja Kallas — Russia warned that EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas’s participation in Ukraine peace negotiations would derail the process, accusing her of hostility toward Moscow. The warning came as European leaders sought a role in US-mediated talks and Vladimir Putin proposed preliminary discussions with European envoys. Kallas insists Russia must agree to a ceasefire before negotiations on Europe’s wider security architecture.

Russia Bombards Kyiv Again Hours After Attack Kills Seven — Russia launched another missile attack on Kyiv early Saturday, Nov. 21, setting two residential buildings ablaze in the Podil district. The strike followed a deadly attack that killed seven people and injured 17 a day earlier. The renewed bombardment came after the Trump-Putin-Xi summit in China failed to secure a ceasefire, with Zelensky warning that Trump’s friendly rhetoric toward Putin emboldens Moscow.

As Trump Embraces Putin, Expert Urges Europe to Prepare for War Without US — European security expert Sven Biscop warns that Europe lacks the political command structure needed to fight Russia without US support. In a new Egmont Institute policy brief, he proposes a joint European “War Council” to coordinate military strategy, economic mobilization and crisis responses, warning that fragmented decision-making could lead to disaster in a direct confrontation with Moscow.

Zelensky Honors Young Ukrainian Heroes Who Saved Lives, Raised Millions for Army — President Zelensky honored Ukrainian children for rescuing civilians during Russian attacks, stopping a drone threatening younger siblings and raising millions for Ukraine’s armed forces. Among the recipients was a US citizen supporting 450 Ukrainian military units. Zelensky also discussed efforts to counter Russian intelligence recruitment of teenagers.

Russia Strikes Zaporizhzhia Kindergarten, Injures Civilian — Russian forces struck a kindergarten in Zaporizhzhia overnight Nov. 20-21, sparking a fire in an apartment in a neighboring five-story residential building. Regional authorities reported the attack and began assessing casualties and damage.

Denmark Expels Russian Defense Attaché Over Foiled Plot to Assassinate Ukrainian Rapper — Denmark ordered Russia’s defense attaché to leave within seven days after intelligence officials linked Moscow to a foiled assassination plot targeting Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner. Police intercepted armed suspects minutes before his September concert, while Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen warned of increasingly aggressive Russian operations and pledged stronger support for Ukraine.

Trump Claims Putin Wants Peace as Moscow Rejects NATO-Style Guarantees for Ukraine — President Donald Trump claimed Vladimir Putin wants a diplomatic end to Russia’s war against Ukraine, describing their talks in China as “very good.” However, Trump declined to discuss security guarantees for Kyiv before a peace agreement, while Moscow rejected NATO-style protections despite earlier optimism from US negotiators.

‘For Us, He Is a Killer’: Zelensky Rebukes Trump for Calling Putin a ‘Friend’ — President Volodymyr Zelensky called Vladimir Putin an enemy and a killer, warning that US President Donald Trump’s description of the Russian leader as a “friend” encourages him to continue his war. Zelensky said Putin wants Ukraine destroyed and urged Washington to use its considerable leverage to pressure Moscow.

Russian Strike on Kryvyi Rih Wounds 58, Kills 7-Year-Old and Paramedic — A Russian ballistic missile strike on central Kryvyi Rih, a city in Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk region, on Friday evening, Nov. 20, killed a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic and injured 58 people, including four children, local officials said. Twenty-eight of the injured are in serious condition. Russia struck the same site three more times with jet-powered Shahed drones during the rescue operation. The attack on Pre

Italian Court Orders Child’s Return to Ukraine in First Such Case Under Martial Law — In a first such case under Ukraine’s martial law, a juvenile court in Rome has ordered the immediate return of a 12-year-old Ukrainian girl to her father in Ukraine. Ukraine’s human rights commissioner, Dmytro Lubinets, said on Friday, Nov. 20 that his office had spent six months on the case. The ruling comes months after Kyiv accused Italian courts of blocking the repatriation of Ukrainian children evacuated i

Europe Ready for Moscow Talks if Given Full Role in Negotiations — European leaders are prepared to travel to Moscow for talks on Ukraine if Russia grants them a full role in the peace negotiations, an advisor to French President Emmanuel Macron said on Friday, Nov. 20. The response follows Russian President Vladimir Putin’s invitation to European representatives after his summit with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

Trump Seeks Ukraine Peace Deal Before Democrats Take Over Congress — The Trump administration has told European and Ukrainian officials it wants Kyiv and Moscow to reach a peace deal by early January, before Democrats take control of the US Congress, The Financial Times reported on Friday, Nov. 20, citing four people briefed on the talks. US envoys reportedly conveyed the message during discussions in Moscow, Dublin and Berlin, while Ukrainian authorities fear the rush could force President Volo

Burnham, EU Leaders Agree Deals on Trade, Carbon Markets and Youth Mobility — UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Union (EU) leaders Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa sealed three agreements at a Brussels summit on Friday, Nov. 20, easing food exports, linking emissions-trading schemes and creating a youth mobility scheme. Burnham said the deals would give Britain’s economy a $22 billion boost. However, EU countries said they would hold off implementation until London agrees to cut

Ukraine Launches Flu Vaccination Campaign at Military Training Centers — Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense said Friday, Nov. 20, that the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) have begun their annual flu vaccination campaign. Personnel at training centers and military medical staff would be vaccinated first, with other service members to follow. Mobile teams from the Medical Forces will travel to training centers and ranges on set schedules, aiming to reduce the risk of flu and its complications, including

Dutch Students Protest Military Conscription in 16 Cities — Several thousand students from more than 60 schools and universities walked out of class in 16 Dutch cities on Friday, Nov. 20, to protest a possible return of military conscription, NOS reported. Organized by Stop de Oorlogskoorts and backed by the National Student Union (LSVb), the walkout came a day after a Russian drone damaged the Dutch Embassy in Kyiv amid rising tensions between Moscow and The Hague.

EU Approves €1B for Ukraine’s Drones, Air Defenses — The Council of the EU approved another €1 billion in military assistance for Ukraine on Friday, covering joint purchases of drones, air defense equipment, ammunition and other supplies. Deliveries are scheduled to be completed by the end of 2027. The decisions bring EU support through the European Peace Facility to €11.8 billion and implement part of a broader funding agreement reached in September.

Hungary Lifts Veto on Ukraine’s Final 2 EU Accession Clusters — Hungary has dropped its objections to advancing Ukraine’s final two EU accession negotiating clusters, allowing European Union (EU) ambassadors to approve the screening results. The decision made on Friday, Nov. 20 also applies to Moldova. Both countries must still submit negotiating positions before the EU can formally open the clusters.

Ukraine Child Casualties Hit 4-Year High, UNICEF Warns — At least 114 children were killed and 1,030 injured in Ukraine in the first 10 months of 2026 as figures reach an all-time high since 2022, said UNICEF, the UN children’s agency. Separately, Ukrainian investigators announced war crimes suspicions against three women accused of organizing the deportation of 55 children from the occupied Donetsk region to Russia. Both announcements came on World Children’s Day.

Trump Downplays Russian Incursions Hours Before Missiles Crash in Poland — Trump told Fox News on Thursday that Russian drones and missiles had previously entered Poland by mistake. Hours later, two Russian missiles and a drone fell in southeastern Poland during a large-scale attack on Ukraine. Poland’s defense minister said Warsaw and its NATO partners suspected a deliberate provocation.

Putin Urges Ukrainians to Unite With Russia, ‘Choose Right Side of History’ — Russian President Vladimir Putin has called on Ukrainians to “choose the right side of history” and move closer to Russia, claiming that Ukraine’s leadership is responsible for the country’s decline. The remarks, showcased in an interview, came amid one of Russia’s largest assaults across Ukraine close to five years into its full-scale invasion, and weeks after the UN announced unprecedented civilian death tolls.

Russia Fast-Tracks Crimea Road Funds After Bridge Strikes — Russia will release up to 20 billion rubles for highway construction and repairs along its land route to occupied Crimea before the end of 2026. Up to half will fund a bypass around Mariupol, with the remainder allocated to three sections in occupied Zaporizhzhia region. The decision comes as Ukrainian strikes disrupt the Crimean Bridge and bad weather limits alternative crossings.

Russia Rejects NATO-Style Security Guarantees for Ukraine — Russia has rejected proposals for NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine, calling any arrangements resembling the country’s membership in the alliance unacceptable. The statement contradicts recent claims by US envoy Jared Kushner that Washington had made the Kremlin comfortable with guarantees based on NATO’s Article 5. The disagreement follows negotiations in Berlin where security arrangements and a potential peace settlement were

US Asked Trump-Putin-Xi Summit to Drop Ukraine Clause From ‘Peace Declaration,’ Stubb Says — A Ukraine clause was removed from a joint declaration adopted by Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping after Washington requested its deletion, Finnish President Alexander Stubb said. The final document made no mention of Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Russia Resumes Limited Passenger Rail Service Across Crimean Bridge — Russian-installed authorities in occupied Crimea restored limited passenger rail service across the Crimean Bridge on Thursday after three days of Ukrainian drone and missile strikes. Trains are running slowly and are crowded, the shipping channel beneath the bridge is largely blocked by wreckage, and storms on Friday halted all ferry traffic, including a new emergency passenger service using river boats.

Russian Kh-101 Missiles Crash Near Training Coalition Troops in Poland — Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz confirmed that two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in southeastern Poland during Russia’s massive aerial attack on Ukraine overnight into Friday. The incidents prompted an emergency response, airspace monitoring by Polish and allied aircraft, and temporary flight restrictions at Rzeszow Airport.

Zelensky Urges Pentagon to Unblock Patriot Deliveries — President Volodymyr Zelensky urged the Pentagon to release expected PAC-2 and PAC-3 Patriot missile deliveries on Nov. 20, after discussing the issue with Ukraine’s defense minister. His appeal follows October complaints about US approvals for supplies already paid for by allies, and reports that PAC-3 transfers were delayed while PAC-2 shipments continued. Kyiv is seeking missiles from existing stockpiles to meet its immediate air defense

Estonia Urges Putin to Agree to Ukraine Ceasefire, Rejects ‘Kremlin Tourism’ — Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said Russia must agree to a ceasefire before talks on a lasting peace can begin, dismissing the idea of European leaders traveling to Moscow as “Kremlin tourism.” He urged Europe to reject Putin’s demands, including that Finland leave NATO, and to keep up sanctions and support for Ukraine. His remarks came after Donald Trump urged European leaders to speak directly with Putin.

Odesa Trams, Trolleybuses Halt as Russian Strike Cuts Power — A Russian strike caused widespread power outages in Odesa and surrounding areas on Nov. 20, prompting the suspension of all trams and trolleybuses. Regional authorities separately reported more than 41,000 customers without electricity after a DTEK facility was hit. Across Ukraine, nuclear plants reduced output and emergency outages were introduced after attacks damaged power stations and electricity networks.

Ukrainian Drones Hit Key Russian Oil Hub 1,300 Kilometers From Ukraine — Ukrainian drones reportedly struck the Kaleykino oil pumping station in Tatarstan, a major hub in Russia's pipeline network, damaging oil storage tanks. Separate drone attacks were reported in Kursk, where buildings and vehicles were damaged.

Ukraine Should Recognize Kosova — Prime Minister Albin Kurti argues that Kosova’s independence and Russia’s annexation of Crimea are fundamentally different cases. In an exclusive appeal to President Volodymyr Zelensky, he calls on Ukraine to recognize Kosova, reject Putin’s comparisons and strengthen their shared European future.

Was Shenzhen a Backdoor Yalta 2? — The three-way meeting in Shenzhen was billed by many as Yalta 2 – reference to the WWII meeting that divvied up Europe. The fact that the three presidents made little reference to Ukraine, led many to breathe a sigh of relief. The reaction of the US since then suggests that optimism may be misplaced.

Ukraine Hits Back: 3 Russian Missile Launchers Targeted Overnight — Ukraine destroyed one of three Russian ballistic missile launchers and downed 79 cruise missiles during a massive overnight attack, Zelensky said. He accused Putin of using strikes on civilian infrastructure to compensate for Russia’s diplomatic and military setbacks.

NATO for Donbas? US Reportedly Pitches Ukraine a Territorial Trade-Off — The Wall Street Journal reported that Washington has discussed two ways to end the war. One would give Ukraine full NATO membership if it relinquished the part of the Donbas it still controls. The other would freeze fighting along the current front line and give Kyiv treaty-based security guarantees outside the alliance. Kyiv has said it will not cede territory, and Moscow says it will accept no form of NATO membership for

Germany Signals Possible Sanctions Relief for Russia in Ukraine Peace Deal — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has indicated the possibility of the gradual lifting of sanctions against Russia if it agrees to peace talks and makes concessions to Ukraine. He added that the current frontline should be the starting point for discussions on territorial issues.

Russia Fires 84 Cruise Missiles, 404 Drones at Ukraine After Putin’s Retaliation Vow — Russia attacked Kyiv and nine Ukrainian regions with 84 cruise missiles, 404 drones and additional ballistic and Zircon missiles overnight into Friday, the Air Force said. Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi reported eight people killed and 28 injured, including six killed and 15 injured in Kyiv, where strikes damaged three bridges across the Dnipro. Missile and drone impacts were recorded at 23 locations.

Poland Evacuates Rzeszow Airport Tower for First Time During Russian Attack on Ukraine — Poland evacuated its Rzeszow Airport control tower for the first time on Friday, Nov. 20, during a massive Russian attack on Ukraine. Warsaw scrambled military aircraft, suspended airport operations and issued an air-threat warning as authorities investigated possible airspace violations and an explosion in eastern Poland.

Russian Diesel Tankers Arrive in Brazil as Trump’s Fuel Deal With Putin Fails to Deliver to US — Two tankers carrying Russian diesel have arrived in Brazil, while others have diverted toward the Mediterranean, raising further doubts over Trump’s promise to bring 300,000 metric tons of Russian fuel to US buyers.

Putin Gets Trump’s Handshake and Support, but No ‘Yalta-2’ — Pro-Kremlin commentators billed the Shenzhen summit as a “new Yalta.” Its declaration left Ukraine unmentioned. On the flight home, Trump reportedly told European allies that Putin was serious about peace talks, hours after the Russian leader publicly rejected a ceasefire.

US Says It Got Kremlin ‘Comfortable’ With NATO Article 5-Style Security Guarantees for Ukraine — Jared Kushner says Russia is becoming comfortable with security guarantees modeled on NATO’s collective defense clause, but acknowledges lingering skepticism in Moscow. Zelensky insists NATO membership remains Ukraine’s best protection, while Macron calls for reopening the debate on Kyiv’s accession.

Ukraine Targets Russian Explosives Supply Chain in Strike on Fertilizer Giant — The overnight attack triggered an explosion at one of Russia’s largest fertilizer producers. The plant accounts for around 11% of the country’s ammonium nitrate output, a chemical widely used in explosives manufacture. The strike is the latest in Ukraine’s growing campaign against Russia’s chemical industry.

Explosion in Poland Sparks Airspace Breach Probe as Russian Attacks Kill Civilians in Ukraine — Poland investigated a possible airspace violation after an explosion near Chmielek during Russia’s Friday attack on Ukraine. Russian strikes killed 8 people in Kyiv and Lviv, injured dozens others in several regions, and damaged railway infrastructure across Ukraine.

Russian Missiles Kill 7, Wound 17 in Kyiv, Disrupt Power, Water Supply — Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv on Nov. 20 killed 7 people and injured at least 17. The attacks damaged bridges and critical infrastructure, disrupted electricity and water supplies, and caused major traffic disruptions across the capital.

Shoigu’s Ex-Deputy Jailed for 10 Years Over $80M Military Procurement Scandal — A Moscow court sentenced former Russian First Deputy Defense Minister Ruslan Tsalikov, a longtime Sergei Shoigu ally, to 10 years in a high-security penal colony for embezzlement, money laundering, and bribery. He was also fined 500 million rubles and ordered to repay the defense ministry more than 6.5 billion rubles. A separate organized-crime charge was dismissed, and his lawyers said they would appeal.

Europe Calls for Winter Ceasefire, Reaffirms Postwar Troop Plans Despite Putin’s Threats — European leaders urged Russia to halt winter attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure while reaffirming plans for a multinational force despite Putin’s threats. They also called for a Black Sea ceasefire, legally binding security guarantees, and European participation in peace negotiations.
Russian Drone Hits Kharkiv Hospital, Injuring 5 — A Russian drone struck a hospital in Kharkiv, injuring 5 people and damaging more than 50 windows, according to Mayor Ihor Terekhov.

Russia Hits 3 Kyiv Bridges in Overnight Ballistic Attack — Russian ballistic missile strikes damaged Kyiv’s Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi, and South bridges early on Friday, Nov. 20, prompting traffic restrictions as fires broke out across the capital.

Macron Calls to Reopen Ukraine’s NATO Membership Bid in Response to Russia’s Demands — French President Emmanuel Macron called for renewed discussions on Ukraine’s NATO membership, citing Russia’s maximalist demands and Ukraine’s growing military strength. Speaking after the Berlin summit, he urged immediate air defense support and backed European involvement in peace negotiations.

‘We Won’t Allow It Again’: Merz Says Europe Will Not Accept ‘Yalta 2’ — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz rejected a new Yalta-style division of Europe, presenting Berlin summit leaders with pieces of the Berlin Wall as a warning against repeating history. His remarks followed the Trump-Putin-Xi summit, whose peace declaration omitted Ukraine.

Kushner Says Trump Wants Europe ‘By His Side’ on Ukraine — US envoy Jared Kushner said President Donald Trump wants Europe involved in any Ukraine peace agreement rather than imposing a unilateral settlement. Following Berlin talks, Kushner said he and Steve Witkoff conveyed European leaders’ strong and united support for Ukraine to Trump, while signaling progress on NATO-style security guarantees.

UK Pledges to Stand With Ukraine ‘For as Long as It Takes,’ Burnham Says in Berlin — At the Coalition of the Willing summit in Berlin, Burnham said Europe was ready for peace negotiations but would discuss wider European security with Moscow only after Ukraine and Russia reached a peace agreement.
